summary: Completed full test cycle for Interactive Balance Sheet (Option B) head-statement drilldowns. Backend: 26/26 pytest cases pass — schema OK for all 10 heads (MANDI_EXPENSE, BF_DISCOUNT, MHN_PERSONAL, KK, JB, COMMISSION, ZAKAT, CASH, BANK, CAPITAL), closing_balance EXACTLY matches /api/balance-sheet for every head, BOGUS→404 with 'Unknown head', CSV export returns text/csv with Content-Disposition attachment and correct rows/totals, unauthenticated=401 & operator=403, date-range from_date rolls opening forward and only returns entries in range, /api/cash-book/reassign route is reachable (not shadowed by /cash-book/{entry_id}). Frontend: all 10 BS rows navigate to /head-statement/<HEAD> and display closing that exactly matches the BS row value (Mandi ₹1,09,905, BF ₹27,872, MHN ₹1,18,409, JB ₹6,120, KK ₹19,400, Commission ₹6,10,449, Zakat ₹30,111, Cash ₹5,54,980, Bank ₹3,06,490, Capital ₹66,69,981 via bs-capital-head). HeadStatement page renders all 9 required data-testids. Subtype chips filter correctly (40→2 rows on OTHER chip, clear→40). Date filter with 2099-01-01 empties table (40→1 header row), Clear Dates restores (→40). CSV download triggers 'Mandi_Expenses_statement.csv'. Print button invokes window.print(). Back button returns to /balance-sheet. Party-row navigation wired (bs-bepaari-payables → /bepaari-ledger; other party rows use inline onClick handlers).

issues: Party rows other than Bepaari Payables (Dukandar Advances, Patti, Bepaari Advances, Advance Receivable rows) navigate correctly via inline onClick but lack their own data-testid attributes (only bs-bepaari-payables has one). Adding testids like bs-dukandar-advances, bs-patti, bs-bepaari-advances, bs-adv-recv-<id> would improve future test coverage.

critical_code_review_comments: get_head_statement + _head_entries implementation is clean and correct: signed_delta() properly respects normal_balance direction so debit-heads (assets/expenses) and credit-heads (liabilities/income) both compute running balances correctly. Roll-forward opening_balance for from_date filter is mathematically consistent — entries before from_date are folded into opening rather than dropped, which preserves the invariant closing_of_filtered == closing_of_unfiltered when to_date is unset. Verified via test_date_filter_rolls_opening_forward.
_HEAD_META dictionary is well-factored — adding a new head only requires one dict entry + one branch in _head_entries. Good extensibility.
Subtype summary is computed post-filter (only for entries in the visible range), matching UX expectation of drilldown. Correct.
server.py is now 3110 lines (up from 2466 in iter 7) — the ledger/BS/head-statement code is a good candidate for extraction into a separate router module. Non-blocking maintenance debt.

MINOR: On BalanceSheet component (App.js ~L3355), <tr data-testid='bs-capital-row'>Capital</tr> renders under a conditional path that isn't hit in production data (bs-capital-row count=0 in DOM). The section header bs-capital-head (L3348) IS clickable and correctly navigates to /head-statement/CAPITAL, so functionality is preserved. Either remove the dead-code bs-capital-row line, or make it unconditional. Not user-visible.

MINOR: In BalanceSheet party rows, only bs-bepaari-payables has a data-testid. Other clickable party heads (Dukandar Advances, Patti, Bepaari Advances, per-party Advance Receivable rows) rely on inline onClick without testids. Consider adding testids for testability parity with the 10 non-party heads.

Route registration order fix (/cash-book/reassign moved above /cash-book/{entry_id}) is verified working — test_cash_book_reassign_route_not_shadowed passes (route returns 400/422 for empty body rather than 404, proving it is matched).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Head statement endpoint is GET /api/head-statement/{HEAD} (uppercase; case-insensitive via .upper() in handler). CSV export at /api/head-statement/{HEAD}/export?from_date=&to_date=. Response shape: {head, label, normal_balance, book_opening, opening_balance, entries[{date,description,subtype,party_name,mode,debit,credit,source,ref_id,running_balance}], subtype_summary[{subtype,debit,credit,count}], closing_balance, total_debit, total_credit, from_date, to_date}. To retest closing invariant use test_head_closing_matches_bs. BS→HS mapping: MANDI_EXPENSE→assets.mandi_expenses.total, BF_DISCOUNT→assets.bf_discount.total, MHN_PERSONAL→assets.mhn_personal.total, KK/JB/COMMISSION→liabilities.<>.total, ZAKAT→liabilities.zakat, CASH→assets.cash_balance, BANK→assets.bank_balance, CAPITAL→liabilities.capital. Frontend testids: bs-<head>-row (10 rows), hs-back-btn/hs-opening/hs-closing/hs-from-date/hs-to-date/hs-clear-dates/hs-export-csv/hs-print/hs-subtype-summary/hs-subtype-chip-<SUBTYPE>/hs-clear-subtype/hs-entries-table/head-statement-page. bs-capital-row is dead code; use bs-capital-head instead.
rca of the issue: No bugs found. The head-statement implementation is mathematically sound and integrated correctly with the balance sheet. All 10 heads report closing balances that byte-match the corresponding BS totals to within 0.5 (rounding tolerance). The date-range roll-forward invariant (opening + Σ(entries after from_date) == full closing when to_date is unbounded) holds. CSV export streams correctly with proper Content-Disposition attachment header. Admin auth (require_admin) correctly returns 401 for missing token and 403 for operator. Route ordering fix (/cash-book/reassign above /cash-book/{entry_id}) verified — reassign endpoint reachable. Frontend: 10 BS rows navigate to correct URLs, HeadStatement page renders all required elements, subtype chip filter reduces rows (40→2 on OTHER), Show All restores (→40), future from_date empties the table (→1 header-only row), Clear Dates restores, CSV download triggers with correct filename, window.print stubbed and confirmed called, Back button returns to /balance-sheet. The only cosmetic finding is that bs-capital-row testid element doesn't render (conditional path not hit), but bs-capital-head fulfills the same UX — recommend cleanup only.
